newsitem.title: GERMANY: German mortgage banks see new business stagnating.
newsitem.headline: German mortgage banks see new business stagnating.

text.p: Germany's mortgage banks expect a stagnation in new business this year after a record 1996, the Federation of German Mortgage Banks (VDH) said on Wednesday.
Even repeating last year's level of new business would be a success given an expected 2.5 percent decline in construction investment in 1997, VDH chairman Walter Dieck told a news conference.

In the first two months of 1997, new mortgage loan approvals fell 14.4 percent year-on-year to 14.48 billion marks, but that drop was more than offset by a 26.1 percent rise in loans to the public sector to 52.13 billion marks, the VDH said.
New loan approvals for mortgage and public sector loans rose 12.9 percent in 1996 to 279.9 billion marks from 247.9 billion.
The VDH said net issuance of Pfandbrief bonds rose by 12.8 percent to 173.5 billion marks in 1996 from 153.8 billion marks in 1995.
Overall, new loan approvals in the first two months rose by 14.4 percent to 66.61 billion marks.

The VDH said the volume of outstanding Jumbo Pfandbrief bonds -- bonds with a minimum size of 500 million marks -- had reached 130 billion marks by the end of February or almost 10 percent of all outstanding Pfandbrief bonds.
Jumbo Pfandbriefe were first issued in May 1995, giving the Pfandbrief much-needed liquidity.
